catalyst.event: NO DATED EVENT — and that is stated rather than invented. The driver is the gasoline crack spread at 11.81/bbl on 11/11 against 25.39 in October; the re-rating comes as sell-side Q4 numbers are cut into a quarter that contains the collapsed margin. VLO does not report until late January, outside this horizon.
catalyst.action: Short into the declining 20-day at 386-392 — do NOT chase at 379.83. If VLO rolls over from here without tagging the zone the trade simply never fills, which is the acceptable outcome. Size for a 12% adverse move.

thesis: The NY Harbor gasoline crack has halved in two weeks — 25.39/bbl in October to 12.92 in November and 11.81 on 11/11 — because spot gasoline fell 16.4% while WTI fell only 8.2%, so products are dropping faster than the feedstock. That is a 49.1% Oct-to-Nov compression, the worst in the 15 years of data and 2.4x the prior worst (2018, -20.2%), against a 15-year median of -5.7%. Refiner equities rallied straight through it: VLO is +9.6% off its 11/06 low of 346.45 while its primary margin halved, and it remains below a 20-day (389.70) that has crossed beneath its 50-day (399.97).
key_risk: There is no dated catalyst inside the horizon, so this is a margin-cycle short with no scheduled trigger to force repricing — it can drift for weeks. VLO has also beaten estimates three quarters running (+12.3%, +22.7%, +32.2%), so the tape has been rewarded for ignoring bad news on this name. Short equity requires margin, the 2.38 ATR stop is 11.9% away on a 5.08% ATR instrument, and a crude rebound lifts both crack and equity together.
counter_argument: The strongest case against is that gasoline cracks always compress in autumn, so this is calendar rather than news. That is answered with the data rather than dismissed: across 15 years the Oct-to-Nov change has a median of -5.7% and a mean of +0.4%, with the worst prior year at -20.2% in 2018 — 2026 is -49.1% and ranks first worst of fifteen, and the 12.92 level is the third lowest November in the series behind only COVID 2020 and 2018. The second case against is the beat record, which was earned at a 25/bbl crack; the quarter now running contains an 11.81 crack, which is precisely what breaks it.

counter_argument: Two objections; the first is answered, the second is not. ANSWERED — autumn crack compression is seasonal: across 15 years the Oct-to-Nov 3-2-1 change has a median of -2.0% and a mean of +3.1%, worst prior year -15.1% (2019), and 2026 at -25.3% ranks 1st worst of 15, so the move is abnormal rather than calendar. NOT ANSWERED — the $36.34 level is the second-highest November in 15 years against a $19.24 median, so refiners remain very profitable and estimates may not need to fall at all. That is a genuine negative, it is why conviction is 3 rather than 4 and size is 1.5%, and it is the reason this is a reversion trade rather than a distress trade.

thesis: This replaces the stale 406.77 short level from 10/25 with a live one. The entire precious-metals complex is in broad liquidation, and the high-beta members are leading it down: SLV is 52.1% off its high and GDX 30.3%, with GDX falling 91.46 to 81.64 in four sessions (-10.7%) while GLD broke its 365.17 shelf to close at 355.45. GLD now sits below its 20-day (368.78), 50-day (380.91) and 200-day (408.44) simultaneously. The driver is real rates: with the 2-year 98bp above the funds rate the market is pricing hikes, and gold is the asset that loses most directly to rising real yields.
key_risk: Gold is already 30.3% off its high, so a large part of this move has happened and the target at 336.0 sits only 3% above the 300-day low of 326.19 — there is limited room before major support, and shorts into prior lows get squeezed. There is no dated catalyst, short ETF exposure requires margin, and any risk-off shock or a dovish turn in rate expectations reverses gold fastest of anything on this page.
counter_argument: The strongest case against is that gold is deeply oversold with CPI still running 3.7-4.0% YoY, which is the textbook case for owning it. The answer is that gold trades against REAL rates, not nominal inflation: a 2-year yield 98bp above the policy rate with CPI at 4.3% annualised still leaves real short rates rising, and that is the configuration gold falls in. The evidence that this is liquidation rather than an inflation bid is the complex itself — if inflation were driving gold, silver would not be 52% off its high and the miners would not be down 10.7% in four sessions.
